clue.text: Hill's proclamation: the 13 was 9 15

parts.note: Ben is the Scottish word for a mountain or hill, as in Ben Nevis
an edict is an official proclamation or decree

explanation.surface: A quotation from a hill-dweller announcing who someone used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is built from cross-references: 13 is SIXTEENTH and 9/15 is CARDINAL RATZINGER, so it reads 'the sixteenth was Cardinal Ratzinger', the Pope who took this name in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger became Pope in 2005 and chose the papal name Benedict, the sixteenth pontiff so called.

clue.text: Get down to fastening

definitions.meaning: to ... down to a task is to apply oneself to it in earnest
a metal clasp on a belt or shoe strap

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both the idiom for starting serious work and the clasp that fastens a belt.

clue.text: Nymph putting head before instincts

annotationWithheld.why: Nymph putting head before instincts (6): reads N + ERE + ID, but N can only be the head of 'Nymph', so 'Nymph' would be both definition and fodder

clue.text: Circumventing flippant parent, performed as farm worker

indicators.note: to circumvent is to go round, so the second word encloses the first two pieces

parts.note: did means performed, as in did a dance
airy means casual or flippant, as in an airy dismissal
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone acted out a cheeky turn about their mother, playing a milkmaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circumventing' encloses both the following pieces, which sit side by side inside the word for performed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid is a woman employed in the dairy of a farm, milking and making butter.

clue.text: Without a tool for shaping timeless language, there'll be lying here

indicators.note: without here has its old sense of outside, so the tool goes round the letter

parts.note: a chisel is a tool for shaping wood or stone
taken as written

indicators.note: less the T, the usual abbreviation for time

parts.note: a tongue is a language, as in mother tongue

explanation.surface: A carpenter, deprived of a tool and of words, flops down for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'timeless' means losing T, the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise longue is a long upholstered couch on which one reclines, so someone will be lying on it.

clue.text: See 22
Guy greeting gag

parts.note: a guy is a man, referred to as he
ave is the Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: A man's hello turns out to be a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' looks like a noun for a joke, but it is the verb: to retch.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag and to heave both mean to retch, the body's effort to vomit.

clue.text: Storm about organ coming up with echoes

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: to rant is to storm, raging loudly

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the nose is the organ of smell

explanation.surface: A tempest rages around a church organ, sounding up to the rafters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' wants to be the musical kind, in keeping with the storm of sound; it is a body part, reversed by 'coming up' and wrapped by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resonant rings on with deep, reverberating sound, full of echoes.

clue.text: What's afoot at home (home counties)?

parts.note: the words read as an instruction: half of 'home' is HO, and the home counties around London are SE; together those spell a short stocking worn on the foot

explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads as its own instruction: take half of HOme and add SE, the home counties (the counties around London, in south-east England), to get the hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Half hose are socks or short stockings, worn on the foot, so literally what's afoot.

clue.text: Bird and beast (the last in German) recently upgraded

parts.note: the cardinal is a red North American songbird
a rat is a beast
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird and an animal, one ending up German, get promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: Written in 2005, when Cardinal Ratzinger had just been elected Pope, the top rung above cardinal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Ratzinger had just been elected Pope, the one promotion above cardinal, when this puzzle appeared.

clue.text: Boy or girl keeping fool dependant

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the name encloses the fool

parts.note: Val is a name for either sex, short for Valentine or Valerie
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A child shelters a simpleton who relies on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' signals the container; the name can belong to either sex, which is why the clue says 'Boy or girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vassal was a feudal tenant bound to a lord, so a dependant or subordinate.

clue.text: Former limit in a hill is a killer

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a term is a limit or end point
taken as written
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An old boundary up on a hilltop turns out to be deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: An exterminator is one who destroys utterly, such as a pest-control worker, so a killer.

clue.text: The people of Italy?

indicators.note: the question mark tells the solver the people come from Italy's own letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about who the Italians are.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is the only anagram signal: the letters of ITALY rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are ordinary people as opposed to clergy, a fitting sense in a puzzle about the Pope.

clue.text: 6 1/4% is the next problem

indicators.note: a problem is something to be worked out, so the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A percentage sum sets the next exercise in a maths textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Six and a quarter per cent is one part in sixteen, since 100 divided by 16 gives 6.25.

clue.text: Mechanical facilitators for one's sense of place at a dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
your bearings are your sense of where you are, as in lose one's bearings

explanation.surface: Someone needs gadgets to find their way about at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball bearings are steel balls that let parts turn smoothly, helping machinery run with less friction.

clue.text: See 9
Enemy of love kept in prison briefly upon going inside

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, a score written like O

indicators.note: briefly cuts the word right down, to just its first letter
going inside means this piece is put within the other

parts.note: pent means shut up or kept in, as in pent-up
on means upon, as in on the table

explanation.surface: Romance's foe is locked up in jail for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts 'prison' to its first letter; 'going inside' puts the word for upon within the word for kept in.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is one who stands against you, an adversary or enemy.

clue.text: Roar from 11 broadcast — wait for it!

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the remaining letters are sown in a new order

parts.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 down, a killer

explanation.surface: A bellow from a killer goes out on the airwaves: just you wait!
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of ROAR ('from') out of EXTERMINATOR, leaving EXTEMINT, then 'broadcast' rearranges those.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a thing will happen next time is telling someone to wait for it, at a later occasion.

clue.text: Redirection of debts - ¿25, about: it's in Araucaria's very nature

indicators.note: redirection sends the letters along a new route, so they are rearranged

parts.note: dues are debts owed
the mark stands for a pound sign: £25 is a pony in British slang

indicators.note: about means around, so the setter's word goes round the other

parts.note: a setter refers to himself as me, so his possessive gives my
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter muses that rerouting his debts is part of his own true character.
explanation.walkthrough: The ¿ is a garbled pound sign. 'Redirection of' rearranges the debts and the pony; 'about' wraps the setter's possessive round IT. Araucaria is itself a pen name, hence his very nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing under an assumed name is what the setter does, so pseudonymity is in his essential character; a loose, whimsical definition.

clue.text: Raised ceiling in earnings of 1 across

definitions.note: the definition stands for the office held by Benedict, the answer at 1 across

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pay is earnings

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a cap is a ceiling or upper limit, as in a salary cap

explanation.surface: A cap on pay is lifted for a famous figure's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' reverses the ceiling, as this is a down clue; 'in' puts it inside the earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the office held by a Pope, here Benedict at 1 across.

clue.text: Make an exposure about meat

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: A photographer takes a picture of a joint of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to expose or disclose something hidden.

clue.text: Scots success with 'igher temperature to get result?

parts.note: hotter means at a higher temperature, and with its h dropped like 'igher it gives otter
a burn is a result of too high a temperature

explanation.surface: A Scottish triumph comes from turning up the heat, with a dropped aitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'igher shows the H is dropped, so (H)OTTER. Otterburn was a 1388 battle in Northumberland won by the Scots over the English.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Otterburn in 1388 was a Scottish victory over the English, so a Scots success.

clue.text: Picture that is used as cover for periodical …

indicators.note: a cover goes round what it protects, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
a mag, short for magazine, is a periodical

explanation.surface: A photograph serves as the front of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used as cover for' makes the abbreviation for that is wrap the periodical; the trailing dots run on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness.

clue.text: … which name disclosed a machine used in war

indicators.note: disclosed means opened up and laid bare, so the letters are broken apart and rearranged

parts.note: which refers back to the previous clue's answer, the picture

explanation.surface: Continuing on from the picture, its name is revealed as a wartime device.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to 23 across: 'which' is IMAGE, and with N, 'disclosed' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigma was the cipher machine used by Germany in the Second World War.

clue.text: Beast with a 10 inclined to suffer from immobility

parts.note: a stag is a male deer

indicators.note: inclined means tilted, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: 10 is ten

explanation.surface: A deer with a tilted ten-point rack cannot move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclined' rearranges A + TEN to give NATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stay still and inactive, like water that does not flow.

clue.text: Servant's quarter has very little about it

definitions.note: with 's read as is, the definition is the servant herself

indicators.note: about means around, so the small word wraps the letter

parts.note: teeny means very small
W, west, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A maid's room is tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeny was a between-maid, a young servant who helped both cook and housemaid.

clue.text: Lorry also known as produce carrier

indicators.note: produce here is a verb, to make or bring out, so the letters form a new word

explanation.surface: A truck, otherwise called a vegetable van, carries produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' reads as fruit and veg but is the anagram signal for LORRY + AKA. Ark Royal was the name of several Royal Navy aircraft carriers.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Ark Royal was a Royal Navy aircraft carrier, so a carrier in the naval sense.
